title: What Is a Smart Contract? Crypto's Vending Machine Explained (Beginner Guide)
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. A smart contract is code on a blockchain that runs by itself. Here is how it works and where it can go wrong. Sources: EasyCrypto, CoinMarketCap Academy. AI-generated voice.

scenes.head: CODE THAT RUNS ITSELF
scenes.narration: What if a deal could carry itself out, with no bank and no middleman? That is the idea behind a smart contract.

scenes.head: A VENDING MACHINE
scenes.narration: Think of a vending machine. You insert money, pick a snack, and the machine follows its rules and delivers. No clerk needed.

scenes.head: IF THIS, THEN THAT
scenes.narration: A smart contract is a program stored on a blockchain. It uses if-then rules and runs automatically when the conditions are met.

scenes.head: WHERE YOU SEE THEM
scenes.narration: They power decentralized exchanges, N F T marketplaces, and even some supply chain tracking.

scenes.head: HUMANS WRITE THE CODE
scenes.narration: But people write the code, and mistakes happen. Flaws in a contract have led to big losses in decentralized finance.

scenes.head: HARD TO FIX
scenes.narration: Once live, a contract is generally hard to change. Reputable audits help, but they are no guarantee.
